title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page): Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, free profinite of rank 2. It sits as a normal subgroup with quotient S_3 in a group written 𝔖̂^+_{0,3} (also written Ĝ / Γ̂^+_{0,3}). This is the profinite completion of the orbifold fundamental group of the stack quotient [M_{0,3}/S_3], i.e. essentially PSL_2(Ẑ)-type ≅ (Z/2 * Z/3)^, presented by σ_∞ (order 2) and ρ (order 3). Classically Γ(2)/±1 ⊂ PSL_2(Z) with quotient S_3. 𝒢 is the group of automorphisms of 𝔖̂^+_{0,3} inducing the identity on the quotient S_3. Automorphisms fixing σ_∞ have the form u(σ_∞)=σ_∞, u(ρ)=gρ with g ∈ Π̂_{0,3}. The relation (gρ)^3=1 gives gρ(g)ρ^2(g)=1, which is the 3-cycle relation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. Grothendieck calls this the 'condition liminaire'.

This page: for an arbitrary u ∈ 𝒢 (not necessarily fixing σ_∞), the following conditions are equivalent:
- (i) u sends the procyclic subgroup L'_0 = ε_0^Ẑ of 𝔖̂^+ to a conjugate. Here ε_0 is the 'parabolic' element whose square is ℓ_0, like T versus T^2 in PSL_2(Z).
- (ii) u sends L_0 = ℓ_0^Ẑ to a conjugate inside Π̂.
- (iii) The same holds for all three inertia subgroups L_0, L_1, L_∞.
- (iv)/(v) There exist p ∈ Ẑ* and g_0 ∈ Π̂ with u(ε_0) = int(g_0)ε_0^p, respectively u(ℓ_0) = int(g_0)(ℓ_0^p).

The equivalences are routine:
- L_0 = L'_0 ∩ Π.
- u commutes with the outer S_3-action, which permutes the L_i.
- A procyclic subgroup mapped to a conjugate of itself gives a unit exponent.

For u of the form (50), transporting by ρ gives u(ℓ_1) = int(g_1)(ℓ_1^p) with g_1 = gρ(g_0), and u(ℓ_∞) = int(g_∞)(ℓ_∞^p) with g_∞ = gρ(g)ρ^2(g_0). Here ℓ_1 = ρℓ_0ρ^{-1}, etc.

The exponent p = χ(u) ∈ Ẑ* is uniquely determined and called the 'multiplicateur'; it is the cyclotomic character / the λ of GT. The element g_0 is determined modulo L_0 (g_0 ↦ g_0ℓ_0^α). Such u are said to 'respect the loop structure' (structure à lacets). The condition depends only on the outer automorphism class. In the margin he introduces notations Aut_lac, Autext_lac, Aut_lac(·,σ_0), Aut_lac(·,σ_∞), Aut_lac(Π̂_{0,3}).

Purpose: to define the 'inertia-preserving' subgroup of automorphisms. This prepares a description of Ĝ𝒯-type groups as automorphisms of the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) / Π̂_{0,3} preserving the loop structure. It continues (next page) with the parametrization of the solutions g of the 3-cycle relation by two conjugacy classes of order-3 lifts, correlated with p ≡ ±1 mod 3.
errors: Check of the transport formula: u(ρℓ_0ρ^{-1}) = gρ·g_0ℓ_0^pg_0^{-1}·ρ^{-1}g^{-1} = int(gρ(g_0))(ℓ_1^p), so g_1 = gρ(g_0) is correct. Applying once more gives g_∞, and a third application returns g_0 by (51), so the formulas are consistent.
Formula (55) is labelled twice, a numbering slip.
Point (i) is written with ℓ'_0 overlined by ε_0, i.e. a notational hesitation between ℓ'_0 and ε_0.

ideas.what: Automorphisms of the profinite completion of Z/2*Z/3 (PSL_2-type group containing Π̂_{0,3} with quotient S_3) fixing σ_∞ and sending ρ to gρ, with gρ(g)ρ^2(g)=1
ideas.modern_name: 3-cycle (hexagon-type) relation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group ĜT; description of GT via automorphisms of PSL_2(Ẑ)-completion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990); Ihara; Lochak–Schneps (1990s) for the braid/mapping-class group viewpoint
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and the action on π_1 of M_{0,3}/M_{0,4}, without these formulas

ideas.what: Equivalence of preserving one inertia (loop) class versus all three, with a common exponent p ∈ Ẑ*
ideas.modern_name: inertia-preserving (braid-like / 'cyclotomic') outer automorphisms; λ = χ(u) cyclotomic character

ideas.what: g_0 determined modulo the inertia subgroup L_0; transport formulas g_1 = gρ(g_0), g_∞ = gρ(g)ρ^2(g_0)
ideas.modern_name: cocycle data for inertia-preserving automorphisms (the 'f' element up to the centralizer of inertia)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, independent setup of what is now the inertia-preserving / GT-type automorphism framework for (Z/2*Z/3)^ ⊃ Π̂_{0,3}. It is essentially Drinfeld/Ihara material, and the content on this page is routine definitional work. The historically interesting point (independent development, terminology 'condition liminaire', 'multiplicateur', 'structure à lacets') is already known in outline from the Longue Marche context.
transcription_corrections: 'donc pas g' should likely read 'donc par g' (p is determined by u, hence by g, written p = χ(u) when u is given by (50))
The group is the same as 𝔖̂^+_{0,3} of the previous page (rendered here as Ĝ^+_{0,3}). The first line likely reads 'Pour un u ∈ 𝒢 = Aut(𝔖̂^+_{0,3})' ' (ne fixant pas nécessairement σ_∞)'.
In (54)(i), the element is ε_0 (written over ℓ'_0), with ε_0^Ẑ = L'_0.
In the lower part, read 'ou sous-groupes engendrés par' rather than 'sous-entendus par' (uncertain).
